name: pxfer
transitions: real->protected (CR0.PE 0->1, CS far-jump to 32-bit flat code 0x08)

GDT (23 entries): code0 0x08 nonconf DPL0, data0 0x10, code3 0x18, data3 0x20, TSS1 0x28 (LTR'd), CONFORMING DPL1 code 0x30, TSS_A 0x38 (available), LDT desc 0x40 (LDT @ 0x3400 limit 0x07, entry 0 = an AVAILABLE TSS), TSS_NP 0x48 (P=0), call gate 0x50 (P=0), call gate 0x58 (DPL0 -> 0x60), NONCONFORMING DPL1 code 0x60, CONFORMING DPL0 code 0x68, TSS2 0x70 (available), TSS_C 0x80 (available), TSS_D3NP 0x88 (available DPL3 P=0), TSS_B 0x90 (busy P=1), TSS_BNP 0x98 (busy P=0), LDT desc 0xA0 (P=0), task gate 0xA8 (P=0 -> TSS2), task gate 0xB0 (P=1 -> TSS2)
IDT: vectors 10 AND 13 -> gp_entry (SHARED -- QEMU raises #TS where the SDM mandates #GP for case 4; the vector is graded from +ven_faultlog), 11 -> np_entry
CPL0 phase: 13 rejected transfers (cases 1-7 + the combined-invalid matrix cases 14-19) + 3 accepted controls (cases 8-10), then the ACCEPTED task switch (ljmp $0x70) into task2

task2 records the GDT/LDT busy bytes (TSS1 0x89 / TSS2 0x8B toggled by the accepted switch; TSS_A and the LDT-TSS UNTOUCHED at 0x89 by the rejected cases 3/4), then transfers DOWN to CPL3 via an outer RETF

CPL3 phase: 7 more rejected transfers (cases 11-13 + combined-invalid cases 20-23) delivered cross-privilege onto TSS2's SS0:ESP0, then the 9 descriptor-access-byte checks + the witness pull + isa-debug-exit (status 133) at CPL3 (IOPL=3 from the TSS2 image)

cases.1: lcall 0x000B (code0 nonconf DPL0, RPL 3) from CPL0 -> #GP(0x08). Fix rule 1: direct CALL nonconforming needs RPL <= CPL. HEAD accepts and pushes a frame for a run at offset 0
cases.2: ljmp 0x30 (CONFORMING DPL1) from CPL0 -> #GP(0x30). Fix rule 1: conforming needs DPL <= CPL. HEAD had no conforming-DPL rule and transferred
cases.3: RETF popped CS = 0x38 (TSS_A, a SYSTEM descriptor) -> #GP(0x38). Fix rule 3: a RETF may not resolve a system descriptor. HEAD task-switched into TSS_A. ESP preserved (staged advance never fires); TSS_A busy byte stays 0x89
cases.4: ljmp 0x0004 (TSS in LDT entry 0) -> #GP(0x0004) per SDM Vol.3A 8.2.2 (TSS descriptors may only live in the GDT). Fix rule 4 + R2-C02 TI preservation (err 0x0004, not 0x0000). QEMU raises #TS(0x0004) instead -- ORACLE GAP, see oracle_gaps. HEAD accepted the LDT-resident TSS and switched into the garbage TSS at 0x4300
cases.5: ljmp 0x48 (TSS_NP, P=0) -> #NP(0x48). Fix rule 5: a not-present TSS is #NP, not the unsupported-descriptor HALT (HEAD halts)
cases.6: lcall 0x50 (call gate, P=0) -> #NP(0x50). Fix rule 5 (HEAD halts)
cases.7: lcall through gate 0x58 (DPL0) -> 0x60 (nonconf DPL1) from CPL0 -> #GP(0x60) naming the TARGET selector. Fix rule 6. HEAD accepted it as a same-privilege transfer; the probe faults BEFORE any push (ESP witness)
cases.8: ACCEPTED control: ljmp 0x68 (CONFORMING DPL0) succeeds (conf_ok sentinel + jump back). The validator is not a blanket reject
cases.9: ACCEPTED control: lcall 0x08 -> callee9 -> lret, an ordinary same-level CALL/RETF round trip
cases.10: ACCEPTED control: ljmp 0x70 (TSS2, available, GDT, limit 0x67) performs a real task switch (busy toggle 0x89->0x8B / 0x8B->0x89 read back in task2)
cases.11: ljmp 0x08 (nonconf DPL0) from CPL3 -> #GP(0x08). Fix rule 1: DPL == CPL required. HEAD accepted and LOWERED CPL to the selector RPL 0 -- the silent privilege escalation the finding names
cases.12: lcall 0x80 (TSS_C, available, DPL0) from CPL3 -> #GP(0x80). Fix rule 4: TSS transfers need DPL >= max(CPL, RPL). HEAD entered the nesting switch. TSS_C busy byte stays 0x89
cases.13: RETF popped CS = 0x0008 (RPL 0 < CPL 3) -> #GP(0x08). Fix rule 2: a RETF may not raise privilege. HEAD took the same-level path and lowered CPL
cases.14: COMBINED-INVALID: ljmp 0x98 (TSS_BNP: busy 386 TSS, P=0) -> #GP(0x98), NOT #NP. A direct JMP/CALL to the busy type hits the oracle's switch(type) default -- #GP(selector) outright; switch_tss_ra's presence check is never reached for this class (verified in the pinned seg_helper.c). A presence-first dispatcher reports #NP(0x98)
cases.15: control for 14: ljmp 0x90 (TSS_B: busy 386 TSS, P=1) -> #GP(0x90). Same default-case #GP with the presence bit SET: the busy reject is a type rule, not presence
cases.16: COMBINED-INVALID: ljmp 0xA0 (an LDT descriptor with P=0) -> #GP(0xA0), NOT #NP. An LDT descriptor is never a far-transfer target: the oracle's default case is #GP(selector) present or not. A presence-first dispatcher reports #NP(0xA0)
cases.17: control for 16: ljmp 0x40 (the LLDT'd LDT descriptor, P=1) -> #GP(0x40). Same default-case #GP with P=1: the class reject does not consult presence
cases.18: control for 19 (presence-only): ljmp 0xA8 (task gate, P=0, DPL0, RPL0) -> #NP(0xA8). Class and privilege admissible, so the oracle reaches switch_tss_ra's task-gate presence check (EXCP0B on the GATE selector, before the embedded TSS selector is read). Proves case 19 is a precedence result, not a blanket #GP on absent task gates
cases.19: COMBINED-INVALID: ljmp 0x00AB (the same P=0 task gate, selector RPL cranked to 3) -> #GP(0xA8), NOT #NP. Gate DPL(0) < RPL(3): the oracle's helper raises #GP(selector) BEFORE switch_tss_ra's presence check. Error code has RPL cleared (0xA8) in both oracles
cases.20: COMBINED-INVALID: ljmp 0x48 (TSS_NP: available 386 TSS, DPL0, P=0) from CPL3 -> #GP(0x48), NOT #NP. TSS DPL(0) < CPL(3): the helper's DPL arm precedes switch_tss_ra's presence check (case 5 faults the SAME selector #NP from CPL0 -- the privilege rule, not presence, selects the vector here)
cases.21: control for 20 (presence-only): ljmp 0x88 (TSS_D3NP: available 386 TSS, DPL3, P=0) from CPL3 -> #NP(0x88). DPL(3) >= max(CPL(3), RPL(0)), so the oracle reaches switch_tss_ra's presence check: #NP(selector)
cases.22: COMBINED-INVALID (task gate, present): ljmp 0xB0 (task gate, P=1, DPL0 -> TSS2) from CPL3 -> #GP(0xB0). Gate DPL(0) < CPL(3): #GP(gate selector) in the helper BEFORE switch_tss_ra runs. The admissible-DPL form of this transfer is the accept-gap (see accept_gaps) and is deliberately NOT in this image
cases.23: COMBINED-INVALID: lcall 0x50 (call gate, P=0, DPL0) from CPL3 -> #GP(0x50), NOT #NP. Gate DPL(0) < CPL(3): helper_lcall_protected's gate-DPL arm precedes its presence check (case 6 faults the SAME gate #NP from CPL0). The family's presence-only control is case 6 (deduped, not repeated)

witnesses.edi at exit: (nnp<<16)|ngp == 0x0004000F -- four #NP (cases 5,6,18,21) + fifteen #GP (cases 1,2,3,7,11,12,13,14,15,16,17,19,20,22,23), vectors recorded by the handlers into the slot array
witnesses.esi at exit: (c4_ok<<16)|(busy_ok<<8)|esp_ok == 0x00010914 -- case 4 faulted with err 0x0004 (TI preserved, vec in {10 QEMU, 13 SDM/RTL}) AND all 9 descriptor access bytes named by the rejected transfers read back EXACTLY as built (no busy-bit set, no type/presence rewrite: 0x48=0x09, 0x88=0x69, 0x90=0x8B, 0x98=0x0B, 0xA0=0x02, 0xA8=0x05, 0xB0=0x85, 0x40=0x82, 0x50=0x0C) AND every one of the 20 rejected transfers left ESP EXACTLY as it was at the faulting instruction (no stack write: the far-CALL probe faults before the push, the RETF ESP advance is staged, the TSS/gate rejects precede S_TSW_*)
witnesses.ebp at exit: (TSS_A.acc<<8)|TSS_C.acc == 0x00008989 -- the busy bytes of the two available TSS descriptors named by the REJECTED transfers (cases 3,12) are UNTOUCHED: no task switch, no busy-bit write
witnesses.ebx at exit: (TSS1.acc<<8)|TSS2.acc == 0x0000898B -- the ACCEPTED switch (case 10) toggled the busy bits: the JMP-to-valid-TSS control really happened
witnesses.ecx at exit: (case1.err<<16)|case12.err == 0x00080080 -- the handler-recorded error codes name the rejected selectors
witnesses.0x200c: LDT-TSS access byte == 0x89 (read back in task2): case 4's rejected transfer wrote no busy bit (differential-checked in the trace; HEAD switches into it and diverges long before)
witnesses.0x2020/0x2024/0x201c: 0xC0F0C0F0 / 0x9CAC9CAC / 0xCA11E900 -- the ACCEPTED controls (cases 8,9) really transferred and returned (differential-checked in the trace)

oracle_gaps: case 4 (direct JMP to an LDT-resident TSS, selector 0x0004): QEMU 8.2.2 raises #TS(0x0004) (switch_tss_ra's `tss_selector & 4` check fires #TS for direct jumps and IRET returns alike). SDM Vol.3A 8.2.2 'TSS Descriptor': an access to a TSS through a TI-set selector 'causes a general-protection exception (#GP) ... during CALLs and JMPs; it causes an invalid TSS exception (#TS) during IRETs'. The RTL fix follows the SDM (#GP(0x0004), TI preserved). The flows are made IDENTICAL for the differential by routing IDT vectors 10 and 13 to the SAME handler entry (the pssiret precedent): the error code (0x0004) and the ESP-at-fault agree in both oracles, so the traces match record-for-record; the VECTOR NUMBER is graded directly from the RTL +ven_faultlog in run-sys-golden.sh (vec=13 err=00000004 exactly once, vec=10 never), so the sharing cannot hide a wrong vector
accept_gaps: task gate / 286 TSS with P=1 and admissible DPL (e.g. ljmp 0xB0 from CPL0, or 0xA8 with P=1): QEMU ACCEPTS the transfer -- switch_tss_ra resolves the gate's embedded TSS selector and performs the switch (verified in the pinned seg_helper.c). This core does not implement the task-gate/286-TSS forms and loud-HALTs (docs/unsupported-isa.md), but only AFTER every architecturally required fault has been selected (RETF-kind #GP, DPL #GP, busy #GP, absent #NP). The shape is therefore NOT differentially expressible and is deliberately absent from this image: every faulting form that precedes the accept IS covered (cases 18, 19, 22 for the task gate; the TSS forms by cases 5, 10, 12, 14, 15, 20, 21), and the halt itself is unreachable from any legal fault-free transfer this image performs

description: REVIEW1_Aug3 R2-C01 regression: S_LJMP must validate far transfers PER KIND, plus the system-descriptor dispatch precedence matrix (TYPE/DPL classification BEFORE PRESENCE, the pinned oracle's order). Twenty rejected transfers + three accepted controls in one image, all differential against QEMU 8.2.2 (which implements every rule -- verified in the pinned harness seg_helper.c), except the one documented oracle gap (case 4: QEMU #TS vs SDM #GP for a direct JMP to an LDT-resident TSS, bridged by the pssiret shared-handler pattern + +ven_faultlog vector grading). CPL0 phase: direct CALL with RPL>CPL (#GP), direct JMP to conforming DPL>CPL (#GP), RETF to a system (TSS) descriptor (#GP), JMP to an LDT-resident TSS (#GP/#TS, err 0x0004 TI preserved), JMP to a not-present TSS (#NP), CALL through a not-present call gate (#NP), CALL through a gate to a nonconforming DPL>CPL target (#GP(target)), and the combined-invalid matrix: JMP to a busy TSS with P=0 (#GP, not #NP; present-busy control), JMP to an LDT descriptor with P=0 (#GP, not #NP; present-LDT control), JMP to a not-present task gate (#NP) vs the same gate with RPL>DPL (#GP). Accepted controls: direct JMP to conforming DPL==CPL, an ordinary same-level CALL/RETF, and a JMP to a valid available TSS (a real task switch whose busy toggle is read back in the incoming task). CPL3 phase (after an outer RETF in the switched-in task): direct JMP to nonconforming DPL<CPL (#GP), CALL to a TSS with DPL<CPL (#GP), RETF with popped RPL<CPL (#GP), JMP to a not-present TSS with DPL<CPL (#GP, not #NP; the DPL3 presence-only control #NP), JMP to a present task gate with gate DPL<CPL (#GP), CALL through a not-present call gate with gate DPL<CPL (#GP, not #NP; the CPL0 case is the presence-only control). Every rejected transfer is additionally witnessed to have performed NO stack write (ESP at the fault, handler-recorded and mainline-verified), NO busy-bit write and NO descriptor-byte rewrite (the named descriptors' access bytes read back exactly as built). The witnesses are pulled into the GPRs before the isa-debug-exit so the run-sys-golden.sh step-7 RTL sys-diff compares them record-for-record and step-5f asserts them. The one accept-gap (task gate / 286 TSS with P=1 + admissible DPL: QEMU switches, this core loud-HALTs after the faults) is documented in accept_gaps and deliberately not in the image. NO paging (the validation rules are paging-independent; the paged selector/nullness defects are pselnull's).
